hints.content:
The point $(-2,-3)$ lies in the shaded area of one of the inequalities, but *not* in the shaded area of both.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a graphed system of inequalities. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. There is a solid line representing an inequality that goes through the points zero, four and one, one. The shaded region for the inequality is below the line. There is another solid line representing the second inequality that goes through the points zero, negative one and four, negative four. The shaded region for this inequality is above the line. The point negative two, negative three is plotted inside the shaded region of one of the inequalities.

hints.content: No, $(-2,-3)$ is not a solution of the system of inequalities.
